open_questions: Sector 70 shows negative depth -202 ppm and epochs -30 and 0 show -26 and -9 ppm – confirmation with ground-based photometry and a cleaner TESS aperture is needed to verify the ~510 ppm average depth.
Duration ratio 1.406 (observed_h 4.997 vs central_h 3.554) implies a grazing geometry (fit_b 0.9859) – radial velocities and higher-SNR transits would tighten density and radius.
dossier.public_summary: A shallow ~510 ppm dip repeats every 13.1 days with a flat bottom that implies a ~1.9 Earth-radius planet around a K dwarf 80 parsecs away. The dip depth jumps from sector to sector and between individual transits, and the star itself varies by 4,000-17,000 ppm at about 6.4 days – about half the transit period – making individual events noisy and a few transits atypical. No odd-even difference, secondary eclipse, off-target centroid, or nearby star capable of mimicking the dip was found, leaving a planet as the best explanation despite the variability.

reasons.why: Transit depth gives a 1.91 R_earth planet if on target, well below the 10 R_earth threshold; flat-ish shape (shape.v_sigma 1.719) favours a planet over V-shaped binary.
No star within 1 TESS pixel can cause the 510 ppm dip with a reasonable eclipse, and difference imaging has no secure off-target or neighbour detection.

reasons.why: No significant odd-even depth difference and no secondary eclipse meets the >5 snr criterion for an eclipsing binary on the target.

Depth changes between sectors and transits are extreme, but transit_depths shows the signal is driven by a few outliers (1760,1303 ppm; -202, -26, -9 ppm) and the reported depth_change_pct 244.7 reflects spot+aperture leakage on this highly variable star rather than a binary nodding signal.

reasons.why: Star is strongly variable (amplitude_ppm >> depth) and the period is ~2x the spin period, as expected for chance alignment and spot harmonics; with no phase_curve swing (amplitude_ppm 67.61 ratio_to_depth 0.1326) this does not favor a stellar binary, while the xgboost planet_rank 0.06 is low because variability dominates the checker.
